monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a quiet fever that makes my flat edges feel too thin. I stand on The Bottom-Heavy Stand, where the wide rock presses against a fence that leans wrong. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Did the air above me become heavy like a lid, or is it just empty space pressing down? I set down a fence beside the stand, testing if the memory of stone can catch the slip while the heat rises. I press the wide rock where the flat line slips, hoping the stand holds the fever while the chest waits nearby. If the air feels thin, I will keep pressing until the wrong shape becomes real.
